About Event

Fast Forward is a one-day hackathon for builders creating what comes next: useful agents, multimodal AI apps, and immersive VR experiences.
Join Vercel + Meta , with support from integration partners Shopify and Neon Postgres , on Wednesday, October 14, from 10am–6pm in San Francisco . Build, experiment, and turn an idea into a working demo with mentor support, team collaboration, and live finalist presentations.
Choose your track
Agents & Factories: Build agents that keep producing useful work after you step away. Think research assistants, automated workflows, and systems that turn information into action.

Multi-modal Apps: Combine text, images, voice, and multiple AI models to create new ways to interact with software.

VR Apps: Build immersive web experiences with v0 and Meta’s WebXR tools.

Optional challenges (for chance to win prizes):
Build with commerce - build with a commerce experience in mind using Shopify Catalog, from product discovery to a shopping agent, for a chance to win an additional prize. Open to builders across all three tracks.

Race against a model - play an exclusive Vercel racing game, race against AI models (and win) for a chance to win prizes while supplies last.

What to expect
A full day of building, snacks and lunch, mentor support, and a chance to share what you’ve made. Come with a team or meet collaborators during team formation.

Program
Yury Selivanov, MTS, Vercel | what you can build with full-stack and AI apps on Vercel today.

Meta | delightful VR experiences

Andre Landgraf | building AI apps and Agents on Neon

Demos, judging, and prizes
Submit your project by 4pm , including a working demo link, a short description, your team roster, and any setup instructions. Select one award track.
Judges will review submissions and select nine finalists, three per track . Each finalist team gets three minutes to demo live , followed by final deliberation and one winning team per track.
Compete for up to $55,200 in winner credits across all three tracks : $4,600 per winning team member, for up to four members per winning team.

About Event

The Fincantieri Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon comes to San Francisco, October 16–18.

Following the first edition in Rome, which brought together 70+ participants, including Italian Navy engineers, and produced five working prototypes, the challenge now crosses the Atlantic to the Bay Area’s deep-tech ecosystem.
Over 36 hours, engineers, developers, founders, researchers, and designers will form teams to build working solutions around real maritime and defense engineering challenges , with access to technical mentors, development hardware, and potential opportunities to continue developing the strongest concepts beyond the event.
Challenge Tracks
OT Cybersecurity & Blast Radius Analysis - How do you stop one compromised system from taking down an entire ship?

Piping Layout Optimization - Can algorithms find better piping and cable layouts than traditional engineering workflows?

Software-Defined Vessel - What if ships could upgrade and change missions as easily as software platforms?

Build with Real Hardware
Participants will have access to a selection of Qualcomm and Arduino technologies during the hackathon, including Snapdragon-powered laptops, edge AI and robotics development platforms, Arduino prototyping hardware, and supporting developer tools.
These tools are intended for hands-on technical development . Participants with experience in areas such as software development, embedded systems, electronics, robotics, edge AI, computer vision, or hardware prototyping will be best positioned to take full advantage of them.
Qualcomm and Arduino technologies will be introduced during the opening session so teams can quickly understand the available resources and integrate hardware, edge AI, computer vision, sensors, or robotics into their prototypes.
Exact hardware configurations will be shared with participants ahead of the event.

Questions? Join our Discord!
Ask questions about the event, connect with other participants, form a team, receive event announcements, and stay up to date throughout the hackathon.
👉 Join here: OFFICIAL DISCORD CHANNEL
More Than a 36-Hour Hackathon
The goal is not only to build a prototype, but to identify ideas with the potential to continue developing after the event.
Work on real Fincantieri challenges with potential relevance to future maritime and defense applications.

Compete for a Qualcomm-powered laptop awarded to the winning team (Approximate Retail Value: $1,200 USD).

Develop your concept beyond the hackathon: selected promising prototypes may have the opportunity to continue evolving.

Access Fincantieri expertise: winning and particularly promising concepts may receive mentoring from Fincantieri’s network of experts to help further mature the solution and explore its potential application within Fincantieri.

Connect with leading technical talent from industry, academia, venture capital, and the defense innovation ecosystem.

Partners & Ecosystem
The hackathon is powered by Fincantieri , Mind The Bridge and Silicon Mountain .
Qualcomm is the main technology sponsor, supporting participants with hardware, development resources, and technology expertise throughout the event.

Ecosystem Partners:

Berkeley Gateway Accelerator
Berkeley Institute for Security and Governance
Mission Applied Berkeley
Gordian Knot Center for National Security Innovation
SF Climate Tech Club
Bay Area Ocean Cluster
FLEETWERX
Hustle Hours
Additional experts from Fincantieri, academia, industry, venture capital, and the defense innovation ecosystem will support teams through mentoring and judging.

Full details regarding participation rules, eligibility, and data privacy can be found in our Terms and Conditions .
What to Expect
36 hours of hands-on building and prototyping.

Real technical challenges provided by Fincantieri.

Access to Qualcomm and Arduino hardware and development resources.

Mentors and domain experts supporting teams throughout the event.

Collaboration with engineers, founders, and researchers.

A Qualcomm-powered laptop prize for the winning team.

Potential follow-on development opportunities for the most promising concepts.

No maritime background is required. However, this is a hands-on technical hackathon , and participants should be ready to contribute directly through software development, AI/ML, embedded systems, cybersecurity, robotics, engineering, CAD/optimization, product design, or prototyping.
Come with a team or find one at the event.
Spots are limited — register early to secure your place. Registration will close on October 15.

About Event

Space is limited and is mandatory to register on https://events.builder.aws.com/EARgN9 (required to enter the AWS building) and join the discord: Join Discord Server
All guests must be 18+ and present a valid government-issued physical photo ID at check-in (digital IDs will not be accepted). Scooters and bikes are not permitted in any Amazon building with no on-site parking available.
Exciting prizes of 10K+ in credits and cash

The Universal Celebration Hackathon is a celebration of creativity, entrepreneurship, and the next generation of AI-powered companies. Bring your ideas, experiment with new possibilities, and turn your vision into something real.
This hackathon is about more than building prototypes, chatbots, or collections of AI agents. It’s about imagining what happens when AI agents become a team of digital people who can collaborate, communicate, make decisions, and perform real-world work together.
The Challenge
Build an AI-powered company, business, or organization run by a team of AI agents.
Your challenge is to create an AI-native business that demonstrates how multiple specialized agents can work together in a practical, real-world use case.
Think beyond a conventional startup team. Your agents could run a restaurant, manage a retail shop, operate a travel agency, coordinate social services, produce a film, or build an entirely new kind of business.
Each agent should have a distinct role, responsibility, personality, and character. Give them avatars and voices, and demonstrate how they interact with one another, exchange information, delegate tasks, make decisions, and work toward a shared goal.
The agents should do more than talk. They should use tools, conduct research, automate workflows, execute tasks, manage business operations, and deliver tangible outcomes.
The key question is:
What happens when you give a team of AI agents a real-world mission, distinct identities, and the tools to get the job done?
What to Build
Build a working prototype of a real-world operation powered by a team of collaborating AI agents.
Your project should:
Solve a real problem: Identify a practical need, business opportunity, or community challenge.

Create at least five AI agents: Give each agent a distinct role, responsibility, character, avatar, and voice.

Demonstrate real interactions: Show agents communicating, sharing context, coordinating responsibilities, and making decisions together.

Operate in a real-world use case: Demonstrate your agents performing actual business or organizational tasks, rather than simply discussing what they could do.

Use tools and automation: Enable agents to conduct browser-based and deep research, execute code in a sandbox, and automate workflows.

Build with reliability and security: Include code review, code-quality checks, and security vulnerability detection and remediation as part of your development workflow.

Show business value: Explain how your AI-powered company delivers value, serves customers or communities, and could grow over time.

Your agents might include a CEO, product manager, engineer, marketer, salesperson, finance specialist, or customer-support representative. Alternatively, they could be a chef, restaurant manager, inventory coordinator, and customer-service team working together to run a restaurant.
The roles should make sense for the real-world operation you choose.
Choose one or multiple tracks and build your company within them.
Tracks
Climate, Sustainability & Impact
Build AI solutions for a healthier planet and stronger communities.
Examples: climate, sustainability, agriculture, disaster response, smart cities, social impact.
Health, Wellness & Care
Build AI solutions that improve health, wellbeing, and quality of life.
Examples: healthcare, fitness, nutrition, mental wellness, elder care.
Education, Learning & Research
Build AI solutions that make learning, education, and research better.
Examples: tutoring, personalized learning, professional training, research, career development.
Business, Growth & Productivity
Build AI solutions that help businesses work smarter, grow faster, and operate better.
Examples: sales, marketing, CRM, analytics, productivity, automation, business operations.
Media, Entertainment & Creators
Build AI solutions for creativity, entertainment, and digital experiences.
Examples: film, music, gaming, content creation, creator tools, social media.
Commerce, Retail & Consumer
Build AI solutions that transform how people shop and how businesses sell.
Examples: e-commerce, marketplaces, retail, logistics, inventory, personalized shopping.

The Universal Celebration Hackathon is a celebration of creativity, entrepreneurship, and the next generation of AI-powered companies. Bring your ideas, experiment with new possibilities, and turn your vision into something real.
This hackathon is about more than building prototypes, chatbots, or collections of AI agents. It’s about imagining what happens when AI agents become a team of digital people who can collaborate, communicate, make decisions, and perform real-world work together.
The Challenge
Build an AI-powered company, business, or organization run by a team of AI agents.
Your challenge is to create an AI-native business that demonstrates how multiple specialized agents can work together in a practical, real-world use case.
Think beyond a conventional startup team. Your agents could run a restaurant, manage a retail shop, operate a travel agency, coordinate social services, produce a film, or build an entirely new kind of business.
Each agent should have a distinct role, responsibility, personality, and character. Give them avatars and voices, and demonstrate how they interact with one another, exchange information, delegate tasks, make decisions, and work toward a shared goal.
The agents should do more than talk. They should use tools, conduct research, automate workflows, execute tasks, manage business operations, and deliver tangible outcomes.
The key question is:
What happens when you give a team of AI agents a real-world mission, distinct identities, and the tools to get the job done?
What to Build
Build a working prototype of a real-world operation powered by a team of collaborating AI agents.
Your project should:
Solve a real problem: Identify a practical need, business opportunity, or community challenge.
Create at least five AI agents: Give each agent a distinct role, responsibility, character, avatar, and voice.
Demonstrate real interactions: Show agents communicating, sharing context, coordinating responsibilities, and making decisions together.
Operate in a real-world use case: Demonstrate your agents performing actual business or organizational tasks, rather than simply discussing what they could do.
Use tools and automation: Enable agents to conduct browser-based and deep research, execute code in a sandbox, and automate workflows.
Build with reliability and security: Include code review, code-quality checks, and security vulnerability detection and remediation as part of your development workflow.
Show business value: Explain how your AI-powered company delivers value, serves customers or communities, and could grow over time.

Build what’s next. Ship what matters.
Join us in San Francisco for The Build: Hackathon , a one-day gathering of engineers, AI builders, founders, product leaders, and technology professionals coming together to build real products around the challenges shaping the future of technology.
This is not just about building a prototype. It’s about taking an idea from concept to working product in one intense day.
Whether you’re building AI applications, intelligent agents, developer tools, enterprise workflows, data products, automation, or entirely new ideas, The Build is your opportunity to collaborate with some of the best builders in San Francisco, learn from industry experts, and put your work in front of experienced judges.
Event Details
When: 9:30 AM – 7:00 PM, 14 October 2026
Where: San Francisco, CA
Who: Software Engineers, AI Engineers, Founders, Product Managers, Data Scientists, Designers, and Technology Professionals
Format: One-day, in-person hackathon
Theme: Open-ended — build something meaningful
What to Expect
An intensive one-day building experience

Build real products from idea to working prototype

Collaborate with engineers, founders, and product leaders

Mentorship from experienced industry professionals

Access to tools, platforms, APIs, and developer resources from our partners

Live demos in front of judges and industry experts

Networking with San Francisco’s technology and startup community

Food, refreshments, swag, and prizes

Sponsor challenges, awards, and special opportunities

What Can You Build?
There are no limits to what you can build.
Create an AI application, autonomous agent, developer tool, enterprise workflow, data platform, automation system, productivity product, or something completely new.
The goal is simple: identify a problem, build a solution, and ship it.
You don't need to arrive with a finished idea. Come with a problem you want to solve, a technology you want to experiment with, or simply the desire to build alongside great people.
Who Should Join?
The Build is designed for people who love creating things.
Whether you're an experienced engineer, an AI practitioner experimenting with agents, a founder validating a new idea, a product manager looking to prototype, or a developer who simply wants to spend a day building something ambitious, you're welcome.
Come to learn, build, collaborate, and ship.

About Event

Yummy Future Hackathon Festival
Presented by Yummy Future · Sponsored by AWS
📅 October 24, 2026
📍 South Bay + Online Worldwide
☕ Sip. 🤝 Meet. 🛠️ Build. 🏆 Compete.
Your next teammate might be one coffee away.
For three days, Yummy Future brings together the energy of a café, the curiosity of a demo floor, and the excitement of a hackathon. Explore new tools, meet the people behind them, collect Mission Card stamps, and turn a useful idea into something you can show.
Come with a team or find one here. Bring a problem from work, your neighborhood, or everyday life. Local businesses are welcome to share the challenges they would love someone to solve.
Join us in the South Bay—or build alongside us from anywhere in the world.
🎟️ Your Mission Card: A Festival Passport
Pick up your Mission Card at check-in and make your way through the café: meet people at the challenge boards, ask a question at a sponsor station, share what you are building, and collect stamps as you complete your missions.
Every stamp marks a step from “I just arrived” to “Look what we made.”
Here is how the planned on-site missions work:
Day 1 · Find Your People 🤝
Check in, complete your participant profile, and collect your badge → unlock your Coffee Pass .

Complete a verified team-matching action and update your status → unlock your Food Pass .

Register your team, choose a challenge, and submit your one-line idea → qualify for the announced sponsor gift or prize-draw activity.

Day 2 · Make It Work 🛠️
Check in and share your team’s daily plan → unlock your Coffee Pass .

Show a working prototype, meaningful code, an API integration, or another verified build milestone → unlock your Food Pass .

Complete a sponsor integration or put mentor advice into practice → work toward sponsor rewards. Share a 60-second progress video or join a scheduled team interview for additional reward opportunities.

Day 3 · Show What You Made 🏁
Check in and complete your final submission → unlock your Coffee Pass .

Pass your technical check and join your judging room on time → unlock your Food Pass .

Complete your final demo → finish your last mission and qualify for the announced sponsor gift.

Meet someone. Try something. Show your progress. Earn your next unlock.
Mission rewards require staff verification. Menus, quantities, sponsor gifts, and any prize-draw rules will be announced before the event.
🤝 Sponsor Office Hours Throughout the Day
Have a question you would normally leave unanswered? Bring it straight to the people behind the product.
The festival will feature a rolling program of Office Hours across participating sponsor companies during event hours. Each sponsor will have scheduled support slots, with café meeting points and Zoom access for remote participants.
You can:
Explore a product or API through a live walkthrough.

Ask about a challenge, integration, or technical blocker.

Join a short team consultation to work through your next step.

Take that advice back to your build—and turn it into your next Mission Card milestone.

Check the sponsor boards for times and scan the QR code to join the queue. Public Q&A sessions will be recorded; individual team consultations stay private unless the team agrees otherwise.
📺 Live Demos, All Day Long
There is something to follow throughout the event day: sponsor product demos, quick project showcases, team progress updates, and conversations with the people doing the building.
Watch on the café screens, join a scheduled show-and-tell segment, or follow online. Public segments will be livestreamed and recorded, with replays and highlights capturing how projects develop across the weekend.
The early demos are a chance to share work in progress. Sunday’s finalist demos are where teams compete for the awards.
🏆 Chase the Grand Prize
Take your project from a whiteboard conversation to a live demo—and compete for the grand prize.
The planned awards program also includes sponsor challenge awards, recognizing how teams turn technology into useful solutions.
Grand prize details, sponsor prizes, and final award categories are coming soon.
Judges will look at the problem you solve, product execution, originality, meaningful technology integration, business potential, and the clarity of your demo.
🗓️ Your Three-Day Plan
Friday, October 23 · Meet, Match & Get Started
Morning: Check in, pick up your Mission Card, and join the opening and sponsor challenge briefings.
Midday: Explore the Idea Marketplace. Give a 30-second pitch: what do you want to build, and who would you love to build it with? Find collaborators at the challenge and team-matching boards.
Afternoon: Join sponsor Office Hours, explore live demos, and work through your first missions.
Evening: Get mentor feedback, confirm your team and challenge, and register your project idea.
Saturday, October 24 · Build, Play & Make Progress
Morning: Share your team’s daily plan, unlock your coffee, and start building.

About Event

Join us for the Patch the Conference Hackathon, right before GitHub Universe, where we're looking for builders who can find what's broken about conferences and ship the patch. If something about conferences has ever bugged you, this is your chance to build the fix.
Winners take away iPhone Duos, and there are more cool prizes that we'll announce soon. There's plenty of swag for everyone, plus free OpenAI credits to build with.
🗓️ Agenda
9:00 AM: Doors open

9:00 AM to 10:00 AM: Grab breakfast, get set up, start hacking and get familiar with the tools

10:00 AM to 11:00 AM: Workshops and talks from our sponsors to get you up and running

11:00 AM to 2:00 PM: Back to building

2:00 PM: Pizzas arrive, lunch is served

2:00 PM to 6:00 PM: Keep hacking and submit your project

6:00 PM to 7:00 PM: Judging, with teams showcasing their projects on stage

7:00 PM: Winners announced and the iPhone Duos handed over

🛠️ Tools
FalkorDB
FalkorDB is an open-source graph database built for AI agents. Agents are only as good as the context they work with, and a graph gives yours connected data it can reason over, a memory it keeps between sessions, and a clear picture of how things relate.
Here is how you can use it in your project:
Follow connections across data: let your agent answer questions that take more than one hop, with graph queries as its tools.

Remember across sessions: store conversation history and what the agent has learned, so it picks up where it left off.

Share state between agents: give multiple agents one graph to read and write, so handoffs between them work.

Connect people, projects and decisions: bring knowledge from docs, tickets and chats into one graph.

Show the path behind an answer: trace every answer back to the data it came from.

It runs locally with Docker, you query it with Cypher, and it works with Python, Node.js, Java, Rust, Go, PHP and C#.
OpenAI
OpenAI is giving free credits to everyone building at the hackathon, so you can use their models in your project at no cost.
Qodo
Use Qodo in your GitHub repo and it will review your PRs for bugs, logic errors and code quality issues before you merge.
Come solo or form a team of up to 4 people. If you win and don't want the phone, you can take the cash prize instead.

Request to Join

About Event

Build it with OpenAI. Validate with Kane.
Kane CLI Hack Day SF, Supported by OpenAI.
Build it with an agent. Verify it with Kane.
Your agent can write an app in minutes. On October 24 you find out if that app actually works.
We're taking over a room in San Francisco for a full day of building with AI coding agents, with support from OpenAI. Kane CLI runs on OpenAI models under the hood, so for one Saturday the models that help write your code are also the ones checking it.
$30,000+ in prizes and credits
Saturday, October 24 · San Francisco · Hosted by TestMu AI, supported by OpenAI.
Seats are limited and every registration is reviewed. Apply early.
The Challenge
Build a working app with any AI coding agent. Use Kane CLI to prove it works. Ship by 6 PM.
That's all there is to it. Build a tool, a dashboard, a game, an internal utility, a strange experiment, or the side project that's been sitting in your notes app since spring. Just follow two rules:
Kane CLI has to verify your app. At minimum, run it at demo time. The teams that win will go further and put Kane inside the agent: a hook that runs Kane on every save, an agent that reads Kane's NDJSON output and keeps fixing until the flows pass, or a spec that compiles straight into Kane flows.

Your app has to run, ship and survive a live demo. Judges want to see it working in front of them.

Come solo or bring a team of up to four. Bring your laptop and your stack. We'll cover food, coffee, credits and help on the floor.
Pick your track
Web App: The fastest route from idea to verified. Kane CLI works on web apps right out of the box.

Mobile App: Build for iOS or Android and watch Kane test it on real devices through TestMu AI's device cloud.

Wildcard: Anything goes, as long as it ships and Kane can verify it.

Special Prize, Most Innovative Use of Kane CLI: For the team that does something with Kane that we didn't see coming.

The Prizes
🥇 1st Place: Apple Vision Pro + $3,000 in OpenAI credits

🥈 2nd Place: Apple Mac mini + $2,000 in OpenAI credits

🥉 3rd Place: Apple iPad + $1,000 in OpenAI credits

Every winning team also gets:
A 1:1 with the TestMu AI founders

Design partner status, with a say in the Kane CLI roadmap

A featured post on the TestMu blog

A spot on the Kane CLI showcase

A push across TestMu and dev.to channels

Every builder walks away with
$250 in OpenAI credits

3 months of KaneAI Pro (worth $270)

A full day of food, swag, and a room full of people shipping with agents

Before you arrive
Bring the agent you already use. CLI agents, IDE agents, chat agents, MCP setups or one you built yourself all work. Install it and sign in before you get here.

Install Kane CLI and run one flow. Run npm install -g @testmuai/kane-cli and try an example from the docs. A whole room running fresh npm installs at 10:05 AM costs everyone the first hour. Your confirmation email includes a cheat sheet.

Set up your OpenAI API account. Your confirmation email will explain how to claim your $250 in credits.

FAQs
Do I have to build with OpenAI? Participants receive $250 in OpenAI API credits.
Which AI agent should I use? Whichever one you already build with. Terminal agents, IDE agents, browser agents, custom agents, MCP servers and multi-agent setups all count. Kane CLI is the one required layer, and everything above it is your call.
Which other AI tools can I use? Anything that helps you ship. There's no approved-tools list, so bring your own models, frameworks and scaffolding.
Do I need a paid Kane CLI plan? No. Every builder gets 3 months of KaneAI Pro, starting on event day.
Can I bring a project I've already started? Yes, but the Kane CLI integration has to happen on the day. At demo time, show what existed at 10 AM and what you built after that. Judges will weight the new work.
Can I work solo? Absolutely. Solo builders are welcome, and so are teams of up to four.
Do I need to know Playwright or Selenium? No. Kane CLI works in plain English: describe the flow and Kane runs it. If you know Playwright, the built-in export is a nice bonus for your writeup.
What if my project breaks during demos? Test hard before 5 PM, because submissions lock at the deadline and you can't push fixes during demos. If your app depends on a third-party service, keep a recorded run or a backup deploy ready so judges still see what you built.

Request to Join

About Event

🚀Make an impact on real world problems in a single weekend!🚀
HSI is back for our third year in a row! Join Hack for Social Impact once again to tackle real-world challenges . We are teaming up with non-profit partners to present you with important and well-scoped challenges, in partnership with UN Convention to Combat Desertification and 4 local nonprofits.
This event is supported by our sponsors: Gemini, Bild.ai , and Wefunder. Developers will receive credits during the hackathon to work on your projects from our sponsors and technology partners.
$5000 cash prizes in total for the winners of projects
This year, we've teamed up with incredible partners to tackle pressing issues in mental health, climate, justice reform, and art & design:

🌎 Climate : Work with the UN to build an interactive game to enable the community to participate in land planning! Block by Block is a Minecraft-based tool for communities to design their own streets, and has run in 55 countries since 2012. However, it is unsuited to UNCCD's work in real-world land planning: Minecraft has endless resources, arbitrary terrain, and no consequence to player actions. Build a game from real satellite and GIS data showing the impact of land use, to engage the community.
🩷 Mental Health : Boundless Freedom Project can reach people inside with mindfulness and mental health practice through in-person sessions and the Edovo tablets. On release that support falls away, during the 30 days that hit hardest. Build something that keeps familiar practice at hand, holds as little personal information as possible, and assumes no smartphone and no dependable internet.
⚖️ Justice Reform : California's corrections department spends under one percent of its budget on rehabilitation. Transformative Programming Works advocates for them across 120 organizations, but so far can only track process data such as who enrolled and how long a class ran. Join disjoint records such as parole and recidivism data into a framework TPW, and nonprofits generally, can use to track impact.

🎨 Art & Design : BRIDGEGOOD's Oakland studio teaches designers to build with their own communities in mind, through conversations about identity, money and conflict that only work in a small room with a facilitator in it. That room seats a few dozen people a year. Find a way the practice can travel to designers who will never sit in it, without thinning into a slide deck.
🏆 Past winners went to present at UN Climate Conference and build startups that get accepted to YC and raise seed funding!🎯 Will your weekend hack be next year's success story?
✨Register your interest and follow us on our LinkedIn for more Partner & Prize announcements ✨
For more information on the event and a recap of last year, visit our website !
✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨
🤝 Who should sign up? Anyone with a passion to build. Whether you are a technical engineer or a non-technical innovator, if you want to team up with smart, driven people to create positive change, you belong here. Bring your unique skills and the energy to make the world a better place to spend the weekend solving real problems together.
Interested in joining the HSI team? Contact us!
Interested in becoming a sponsor? Contact us!
Interested in work working with our partners? Join the list!

About Event

What’s actually working for AI growth right now?
Building an AI product has never been easier. Getting real users, distribution, and revenue is still hard.
Local Align #3 is a hands-on day for people who want to learn how modern AI products actually grow — from SEO/GEO and organic content to developer growth, community, outbound, automation, and AI-powered GTM.
🎤 Learn from real growth stories.
Hear founders break down how they went from 0 → 1,000+ users , built communities of 10,000+ , and generated millions of organic impressions without relying on paid acquisition.
⚡ Put it into practice.
Choose from 5 real products with 5 different GTM problems — AI DevTools, consumer community, high-trust services, FinTech, and generative AI — and use AI, code, content, or automation to move real metrics: users, leads, signups, traffic, and conversions.
☕ Meet the people building around you.
Not hacking? Come for the talks, startup demos, Coffee Chats, board games, food, and an afternoon with founders, engineers, creators, students, and GTM operators from across the Bay Area.
Come to learn. Come to build. Come to meet your next collaborator, customer, cofounder — or simply someone worth knowing.
You do not need to compete to attend.
🎤 Learn: How Products Actually Grow
No generic startup advice. Hear real 0→1 growth stories from founders and operators who have built audiences, acquired users, and turned distribution into a system.
Lucy Ye — Co-founder & COO, JobWizard.ai
SEO/GEO × Organic Content × AI-Native Growth
Built a 0→1 SEO engine that generated 2M+ Google Search impressions in 2 months , plus 1M+ organic video impressions with zero paid acquisition . Learn how an early-stage AI startup turns search, content, and AI automation into repeatable distribution.
Weijia — Founder & CEO, LingCode
Developer Growth × Product-Led Growth × Community
Built content reaching millions, grew a coding education platform from 0 → 10,000+ students , and took LingCode from launch to 1,000+ users in its first month . Learn how technical founders can turn product, content, and community into an organic growth engine.
More founders & GTM operators to be announced.
⚡ Build: 5 Real Products. 5 Real Growth Problems.
Most hackathons ask you to build another demo.
Here, you'll work on a real product with real users and a real GTM problem — then use AI, code, content, outbound, SEO/GEO, automation, communities, or whatever else you can invent to move the numbers.
💻 AI Developer Tools — LingCode
How do you win developers when every week brings another AI coding tool?
Grow an AI-native IDE through developer communities, technical content, product-led loops, GEO, creators, or your own growth automation.
Learn: developer GTM, PLG, community growth, and how technical products earn adoption.
🎾 Consumer Community — Tennistry
3,500+ users. 1,500+ real tennis matches. How do you create the next 1,000?
Tennistry connects tennis players in real life. Test local acquisition, referrals, ambassadors, events, creators, and ways to prove which users you actually brought in.
Learn: consumer growth, network effects, referral loops, local/community GTM, and attribution.
🇺🇸 High-Trust Services — TurboNIW
How do you acquire customers when the decision is expensive, complex, and built on trust?
TurboNIW helps STEM researchers and professionals prepare for the EB-2 NIW process through structured educational materials and guidance. Unlike a casual app download, customers may spend $1,000+ and are making a high-stakes career decision—making trust and intent central to acquisition. TurboNIW
Learn: high-intent SEO/GEO, trust-based funnels, educational content, lead qualification, and customer acquisition for high-consideration services.
💳 Consumer FinTech — MaxWorth
30,000 users already. What becomes the next scalable growth channel?
MaxWorth is a North American credit-card management app entering its next stage of growth. Explore finance content, SEO/GEO, creators, referrals, communities, partnerships, or new product-led acquisition loops.
Learn: consumer FinTech GTM, lifecycle growth, referral mechanics, content distribution, and scaling beyond early adopters.
🎬 Generative AI × Entertainment — SxeneMixer
A new AI creative product is starting from zero. Where do the first 100 real users come from?
SxeneMixer is an AI short-drama generation platform. Find the creators and communities most likely to care, then experiment with UGC, viral formats, creator seeding, social distribution, and product-led sharing.
Learn: 0→1 launches, creator GTM, UGC, viral loops, and consumer AI distribution.
Pick the problem you want to learn. Build the growth experiment. Run it on a real product. Show us what happened.

More challenges will be revealed.
🏆 $200 cash prize per Challenge
☁️ $3,000+ shared Alibaba Cloud AI/API credits available to participating teams
🛠️ LingCode — IDE Partner & Challenge Owner
☁️ API Sponsor — Alibaba Cloud
Hacker Pass is FREE and requires approval.
☕ Meet: Social, Coffee Chats & Startup Community
Not hacking? You're just as welcome.
Come for:
Founder & GTM talks · Startup booths · Coffee chats · Board games · Food & drinks · Final pitches · New people
You'll meet founders building their first company, engineers exploring what to build next, growth operators sharing what's working, students breaking into AI/startups, and people who simply want to meet interesting people in the Bay Area.
No pitch deck required. No hackathon experience required.

Mobile + XR Track
Create AI-powered experiences for the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra powered by Snapdragon 8 Elite and Samsung Galaxy XR powered by Snapdragon® XR2+ Gen 2 processor, with a focus on mobile intelligence, immersive interaction, and multimodal applications.
IoT Track

Join us for an evening of building, meeting driven founders, and turning bold ideas into real products.
Challenge: Invisible Interfaces
The best interface is sometimes no interface at all. This edition explores products that work through voice, motion, sensors, live data, autonomous agents, and other natural interactions.
Build technology that helps people or systems sense, decide, and act without relying on a traditional app or screen.
1. Dispatch
Use live data such as ship traffic, flight data, fleet GPS, sensors, or border wait times to move physical things where they need to go.
Build for logistics, transportation, ports, emergency response, or defense.
2. No App
Build for people who will never open an app, including seniors, drivers, nurses, warehouse workers, and field crews.
Use voice, phone calls, glasses, vibration, or another invisible interface. If users have to look at a screen, it does not count.
3. Unsupervised
Build agents that run for hours without constant supervision.
Your system should know when it is stuck, overspending, looping, or when it needs to stop.
4. AI-Powered Consumer Products for 1 Billion People
Build an AI-powered consumer product that reaches people through natural, ambient, or invisible interactions.
Rethink how people discover, use, and benefit from technology beyond traditional apps and screens. The strongest ideas will address a clear everyday need and have the potential to serve people at global scale.
Prizes
🥇 1st Place: $2,000 | 🥈 2nd Place: $1,200 | 🥉 3rd Place: $800

Request to Join

About Event

Build It. Test It. Prove It.
Free 3-day Sprint for pre-seed founders. October 21 to 23, SAP Labs, Palo Alto.
Judges from Stanford, Nvidia, Meta, and Microsoft AI spend three days watching how your team actually works, then question you on it. You leave with a clearer next move and a scored record of how you operate, built for investor conversations.
Past teams have gone on to raise from 500 Global and Blitzscaling Ventures and join Berkeley SkyDeck and Confluent's accelerator.
20 team spots. Applications close Oct 14
Judges
Mohammad Rasouli Phd., Researcher, AI for Private Markets, Stanford
Sajal Garg, Principal Soft Eng, Microsoft AI
Abhinav Balasubramanian, AI Lead, Nvidia
Tharun Tej Tammineni, AI Lead, Meta
What this is
Judges who lead AI at Nvidia, Meta, Microsoft AI, and Stanford spend three days watching how your team works, then question you on it. They'll push on your build, your technical claims, and how your team decides. Better here than in a pitch meeting.
You leave with a clearer next move and a scored record of how you operate. Evidence you can bring to investors, not a pitch deck you rehearsed.
Two tracks
Discovery Track. Pre-market, no customer contact yet. For founders seriously exploring a startup, including people inside companies weighing the leap.
Pre-Seed Track. In-market, already talking to customers. Ship something real, show what changed, pressure-test your next move.
What you get
No cash. No trophy. Something more useful.
Teams that clear the Sprint's scoring bar earn the Street Test : 30 days back in the real world, building with no event deadline and no audience, just you and the market. It's a bar, not a ranking. Every team that clears it gets in.
Teams that finish the Street Test receive a Proving Ground report card , a scored record of how you operated across both stages. It covers three things: whether customers are pulling (Pull), whether progress held up after the event (Momentum), and whether this team fits this problem (Founder Fit). It's yours - bring it to investors, accelerators, or a cofounder you're recruiting.
A hackathon ends when the event does. This doesn't.
Schedule
Wednesday, Oct 21: 9am to 8pm. Kickoff, building begins.
Thursday, Oct 22: 9am to 8pm. Full build day.
Friday, Oct 23: 9am to 4pm. Finals, live defense, deliberation, awards.
Who should apply
Pre-seed founders with live customer conversations.
Builders, product leaders, designers, and operators ready to test an idea for real.
University students: the commitment is all three days, Wednesday to Friday, 9am to close. Limited undergrad spots.

Welcome! To join the event, please register below.
Request to Join

About Event

Personal agents can do far more than their demos show. Booking a flight or planning a trip is the stuff you’d happily do yourself.
The web is going agent-native, and most agents aren’t built for it yet.
We think a personal agent should be its own category, not a feature inside a chat app. It should build the interfaces as you need them. And it should deal with businesses agent to agent. Build something we haven't seen before.
What you might build
Think about the endless possibilities:
Your own CFO: runs your entire financial life, from taxes and investments to insurance and negotiating every bill.

Collective bargaining: thousands of personal agents team up to negotiate group rates on rent, insurance or phone plans.

Your agent vs. their agent: buying a car or apartment where your agent negotiates directly with the seller's agent.

A business on the side: an agent that runs your side hustle, sourcing, selling and doing the customer service.

If it’s something you’d dread doing yourself, that’s the right direction.
What to Expect
Hands-on hacking with fellow AI engineers, developers, and researchers

Mentorship and technical support from partner teams and industry experts

API and compute credits to build and experiment.

Food to keep you fueled throughout the day

Live demos and judging with prizes for the top projects

About Event

Hey San Francisco, get ready for a startup pitch competition, investor feedback sessions, and curated networking - happening alongside TechCrunch 2026!
Join us for a high-energy evening where founders take the stage, investors share insights, and global tech leaders connect at Venture Night San Francisco .
Venture Night is part of TechEmbassy’s global event series , connecting ambitious founders, investors, and technology leaders around the world’s major tech conferences.
Expect promising startups, fast-paced pitches, direct investor feedback, and meaningful connections with people building and backing what’s next.

$25,000 in AWS credits from Clowdey and USF

Request to Join

About Event

In this 10+ hour intensive hackathon led by the research team at Obvious you will build your autonomous software factory. TLDR: you'll be able to start assigning your agents features to build instead of prompts.
Note: This event is entirely free, including unlimited tokens for the hackathon. Building and tokens will be using an obvious.ai workspace.
We will be awarding over $30K in token prizes to the teams that can build the most in a day!
1st place receives $20,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

2nd place receives $10,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

3rd place receives $5,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

Come alone or come as a team. If you want to valuemaxx this event (and set yourself up to win big) the ideal group to bring is:
a technical founder or engineering leader

a product manager (if you have one)

1+ engineers (the more ai-pilled the better)

What to bring
Your laptop

Access to a real Github repo you care about [or] a clear vision for a greenfield project

A bug backlog or a list of small improvements

We'll set up your Obvious workspace and go through onboarding in-person. Meals and drinks are provided.
Agenda
10:00 AM – Doors Open
10:30 AM – Opening Session
11:00 AM – Building Begins
12:45 PM – Lunch, with Lightning Talks
3:30 PM – Optional Q&A with Obvious
5:15 PM – Closing Panel
5:45 PM – Awards & Happy Hour
What you’ll be learning:
How to...
design the complete hands-off build loop

manage a multi-pr autonomous agent swarm

prepare more ambitious builds (entire features or even products)

manage QA, code review, and human feedback without slowing down the work

decide where to spend time vs go hands off

rethink both devops and organizational roles in a world of autonomy

scale autonomous software delivery safely

think about roadmap and software design when you can build anything practical in a day

This is for the Engineer & Technical Builder track of our hackathon. If you're interested in learning more about the Product Manager track, check out and register at this Luma: https://luma.com/frontier-builders
What building on the Frontier is like:

-------
About Obvious:
Obvious is an applied AI research lab with a focus on autonomous product development. We spend our days closing the gap between what's possible and what's doable, treating our own company as the experiment for what it means to operate at agent scale. We've reinvented our product, reshaped our team, accelerated revenue, and 10x'd our shipping velocity in less than a year. At peak velocity we've shipped 1000 PRs in one day with 10 engineers.
Frontier is where we do our best to hand that system to other teams. We're excited to work with you!
→ Learn more at obvious.ai/events

About Event

This hack, we're headed back to Studio 45 for a hardware focused hack and build weekend in partnership with Claude Community and other partners.
We're also hosting a warm up build day Oct 17 if you want to join early to make a team and get started on a project.
No pre-reqs. All scientists, software, and hardware engineers welcome.
We welcome all skill levels and can support 50 builders.

Teams will be formed on the spot, and will work through custom automation challenges with sample prep, instrument integration, as well as an open track

⭐️ You must be able to stay through demo on Sunday to participate in the hack . Everyone joining will be expected to demo something by end of the weekend.

Track A: Sample Prep with BioKEA
BioKEA does DNA barcoding, environmental DNA, and long-read genomics from soil, water, or specimen to a verifiable, FAIR-compliant published claim.
They work with open sourced hardware and need help making the sample prep process more robust with a robotic sieving process.
There will also be chances to iterate on other parts of the workcell.
Track B: TBA
We're working with a few different instrument partners and will announce more soon.
Track C: Open build
We'll have extra robotic arms, cameras, and 3d printers for you to build on dexterity challenges or your own problem space.
You can also bring your own hardware.

San Francisco, CA

Registration

Welcome! To join the event, please register below.
Register

About Event

Build a Sovereign AI Model Factory: an ML Engineer Agent that evaluates, fine-tunes, deploys, and improves open models using Union on your cloud.
The best AI teams aren't renting every capability from an external API, they're building systems they own and control. In this hands-on session at the AWS Loft, we'll build exactly that.
We'll start with a walkthrough where we build a LangGraph-powered agent that evaluates open models in parallel, fine-tunes promising candidates, deploys the winner, and retrains automatically when performance drops. Think of it as the first brick in your own model factory : a repeatable system for evaluating, improving, and deploying models you control, not a black box you call and hope for the best.
Along the way, you'll see how Union.ai gives your workflows a durable runtime with infrastructure as context, so agents adapt infra resources, recover from failures, and keep moving without re-running completed work. And because it all runs in your own AWS account , you own the full stack end to end: your models, your data, your infrastructure, your IP.
Then we switch into hack night mode : keep building on the example, bring your own models or datasets, experiment with evals and fine-tuning, extend open models to different parts of your agent, or start something new around the same ideas.
For teams thinking about sovereign AI , this is a practical starting point for owning more of your stack, the weights, the training loop, the evals, and the infrastructure it runs on, all on AWS.
Bring a laptop. Leave with a factory.

All guests must be 18+ and present a valid government-issued physical photo ID at check-in (digital IDs are not accepted). Scooters and bikes are not permitted in any Amazon building, and there is no on-site parking.

About Event

On-Device AI Hackathon: Cleared for Takeoff ✈️
What if you could build an AI application that works, even when the Wi-Fi doesn't?
Your flight is preparing for takeoff. Once the cabin doors close, your connection to the cloud disappears. Before switching to airplane mode, you have one mission: build an AI project that runs entirely on-device.
In this hands-on hackathon from Qualcomm × Liquid AI , you'll team up with a flight crew of up to four people to build with Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) and Qualcomm iQ9s. At the end of the night, we'll turn off the Wi-Fi and put every project to the test.
Will your project survive offline?
Why on-device AI?
Unlike traditional AI applications that depend on cloud servers, on-device AI runs models directly on the user's hardware. That means your product can benefit from:
Low latency ⚡

Greater user privacy 🔒

No server inference costs 💸

Offline functionality 📴

Who this is for
👨‍💻 Developers who want to ship AI features without an inference bill

🤖 ML and AI engineers curious about deploying models beyond the cloud

⚙️ Edge, embedded, and robotics engineers building against real hardware constraints

🚀 Founders and product managers evaluating on-device versus cloud AI

🎓 Students and self-taught builders who want to leave having built something real

You don't need previous on-device development experience. If you can run a script, you can join the flight.
Teams may have up to four people . You can arrive with a team or meet your crew at the event.

STARTUP PHYSICIANS MEETUP | San Francisco
The future of healthcare is being built by physicians. Come spend an evening with the ones doing it.
Maybe you've got an idea you can't stop thinking about. Maybe you're already building and want to trade notes with people who get it. Or maybe you've built, scaled, exited — and you're ready to back the next wave as an investor or mentor.
Wherever you are on the path, you belong in this room.
Join us.
Agenda
6:00 — Welcome & introductions

7:30 — Networking
About Startup Physicians
Startup Physicians is a community of physicians who advise, build, and invest to shape the future of healthcare. We run an incubator that helps physician founders validate their ideas, launch real ventures, and connect with the peers, operators, and capital that turn a clinical insight into a company.
You don't need a finished pitch or a co-founder to belong here — just the conviction that medicine can be built better, and the will to be part of building it.
Speakers
Alison Curfman, MD — CEO, Startup Physicians; Co-founder, Imagine Pediatrics. A physician founder who's walked the path from clinical practice to building and scaling a venture-backed company — and now helps other physicians do the same. www.startupphysicians.com
Michal Nedoszytko, MD, PhD — Clinical AI at Abridge; winner of an Anthropic hackathon. A physician working at the frontier of applied AI in the clinic. Founder of Previsit.ai .

About Event

UC San Diego's Design and Innovation Building hosts Techstars Startup Weekend San Diego, bringing builders, designers, lawyers, and the legally curious together for a weekend focused squarely on legal tech, software, and innovation. The theme: reimagining law for the AI era. The legal industry touches nearly everyone and has changed less than almost any other sector in the last few decades — this weekend is about building the tools that could finally change that, from AI that helps a tenant fight an eviction to software that lets a small business draft a contract without a $400-an-hour phone call.
Around 100 participants will pitch ideas, form teams around the strongest ones, and spend the weekend building toward a final pitch to a panel of judges. Mentors and coaches work alongside teams throughout, helping them get out of the building to validate ideas with real users, sharpen product direction, and prepare a polished final pitch.
Julian Bryant , Lead Organizer of Techstars Startup Weekend San Diego and an attorney/software developer himself, has facilitated roughly 40 Startup Weekends and brings a track record of real companies launched from the format — including CreativeUp, a Santa Barbara-based company that formed at one of his earliest events and is still operating more than six years later.
Jacques Chirazi , Director of the Basement and Entrepreneurship Center at UC San Diego's Office of Innovation and Commercialization, brings UC San Diego's student entrepreneurship ecosystem into the weekend, connecting participants to campus resources that can carry momentum well past Sunday night.
Mason Baldwin : TBD
This isn't just a competition — it's an entrepreneurial laboratory. Participants who've never attempted a startup get to try on different roles — founder, designer, engineer — and learn by doing what Julian calls "experiential education entrepreneurship," packed into three days.

About Event

The Atlantic Stack: Who Funds Europe's Frontier?
Ra's Circle is a private gathering for people who believe the best conversations happen in small rooms.
Each edition brings together a carefully curated mix: investors, founders with exits, policymakers, artists, athletes, and the outliers who don't fit neatly into any category. Never too many of any one kind. Always a balance that makes the room more interesting than the sum of its parts.
It's a rotating circle, never the same room twice, coming together around one question worth going deep on. Real connections. Honest exchange. The kind of conversation that stays with you.
At its core, Ra's Circle is built on an old Silicon Valley instinct that's gotten rare: people who give before they ask. The curious ones, the slightly crazy ones, who believe changing themselves comes before changing the world.
This edition's featured story
Isidro Laso Ballesteros
Senior Official, European Commission · Startups and Scaleups Task Force · EIC Scaleup Europe Fund
Europe has decided it is done watching its best deep tech companies leave to raise their growth rounds somewhere else. Isidro sits at the center of that shift.
He holds two roles at the European Commission. He helps lead the new Startups and Scaleups Task Force, and he helps steer the European Innovation Council's Scaleup Europe Fund. The EIC doesn't just give grants. It co-invests directly in companies alongside venture investors, from early rounds up to large scale-up rounds backed by pension funds and insurers.
Before that, he was an engineer and a two-time founder, then the driving force behind Startup Europe for nearly a decade. During the pandemic he coordinated EUvsVirus, the largest hackathon ever organized: more than 21,000 people built over 2,000 solutions in one weekend.
This evening he joins a small table of space and aerospace founders, investors, and professors in Menlo Park. The question for the night: what does it take to build frontier companies that scale on both sides of the Atlantic, and who funds them when they do?
Come hear the story in person.

About Event

Car AI Navigation Hackathon

Challenge: We have a mini city road with lanes, intersection and traffic signs. Your job is to use AI and a small autonomous car like the Donkeycar or equivalent (typically 1/16th scale or smaller RC car with a Raspberry Pi or equivalent and a camera controlling it) to navigate the "city", obeying signs and making it from one side to the other in the fastest time.

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it.

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what's the fastest way to do it!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it. 

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what's the fastest way to do it!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!

We apologize for any inconvenience and hope you can still join us!
Join the Escondido Creek Conservancy for a special Plant-a-Thon at the beautiful Mountain Meadow Preserve .
Spend the day getting your hands in the soil, surrounded by the beauty of nature, while helping restore and care for our local landscape. Whether you’re an experienced gardener or have never planted before, this is a chance to learn, connect, and make an impact right here in our community.
During the Plant-a-Thon, you’ll help plant native plants, learn about the important role they play in supporting local wildlife and a healthy ecosystem, and discover practical tips and techniques for planting and caring for them. Along the way, take a break from the everyday and immerse yourself in the sights, sounds, and rhythms of the preserve.
Come plant. Come learn. Come connect with nature.
No gardening experience is necessary—just bring your curiosity, enthusiasm, and willingness to get your hands a little dirty!
